newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Newspaper says Israel faces slower growth.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper says Israel faces slower growth.

text.p: Israeli Treasury officials are concerned that the economy will grow less than three percent this year if interest rates do not fall significantly, the daily newspaper Haaretz reported on Wednesday.
Quoting unnamed officials, the newspaper said the fears of further slowdown could prevent the Treasury from making further budget cuts, even if the deficit continues to run over targets.

The Treasury is forecasting a four percent expansion of gross domestic product (GDP) this year, which marks a sharp slowing from the six to seven percent rates Israel has enjoyed most of the decade. Many private sector economists are foprecasting well under four percent for 1997.

The budget deficit for the first two months of the year is running ahead of its targeted 2.8 percent of GDP. The Bank of Israel has urged the Treasury to make cuts immediately, but Finance Minister Dan Meridor has said he will not take any action before the end of the first quarter.

"Only if the Bank of Israel reduces interest rates will we be able to make a budget cut -- assuming one is needed -- without taking into consideration the slowing economy," Haaretz quoted an official as saying.
The officials added, however, that they are not urging Meridor to widen the deficit target.
